lesson.menu_title: Wish You Were Prepared -- Regret, Distance and Desired Reality
lesson.menu_desc: O wish como pedido de mudanca sem reu -- e a hora de NAO usar wish e pedir um mecanismo
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- Wish You Were Prepared
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 12 -- Wish You Were Prepared

listenings.text: There is a sentence English gives you that other languages do not hand over so easily. I wish we had known in June. Say it slowly and notice what it does not contain. There is no subject who failed. There is no verb of accusation. And yet everybody in the room understands exactly what happened, and when. That is not softness, it is precision without a defendant. The moment you say you told us too late, two things happen. The other side stops listening to the content and starts defending the person, and your own credibility narrows to the size of the grievance. I have watched very capable directors lose a year of influence in one sentence. So use the wish for facts about the past. Use it once, keep it short, and follow it immediately with what you are asking for. A regret with no request is just a complaint in a good suit.

There is one form of the wish I use carefully now, and I learned that the hard way. I wish they would tell us earlier is not a regret about the past. It is a judgement on how people behave now, and everyone hears it that way, including the people upstairs. In a group where the head office sits in another country, that sentence travels further than you intended and it arrives without your tone attached. So I made myself a rule. If the thing I want is a fact on the record, I use I wish we had known. If the thing I want is a change in behaviour, I do not use the wish at all. I ask for a mechanism instead: a standing item, an owner, a date. Nobody can take offence at a line on an agenda, and the agenda outlives whoever is annoyed with whom this month.

extra_audio.text: I wish we had known about the reserving gap in June. That is not a grievance, and nobody here needs to explain it. What I am asking for is a standing item on the monthly call. If we hear it early, we course-correct while the correction is still small.

paras: The quarter closed four points below plan, and the reason is not in dispute. What is worth recording is when each of us knew it. The reserving gap was visible in the June data. Nobody hid it. It was simply never a standing item, so it travelled by e-mail, in a paragraph, between two people who each assumed the other would raise a concern.

I wish we had brought the review forward. If only the July call had asked one question about it, the correction would have cost a quarter of what it now costs. Two colleagues have since told me that they had misgivings in June and did not voice them. They gave the numbers the benefit of the doubt, because the alternative was to challenge a market they do not cover. That instinct is decent, and it was expensive.

I want to be exact about what this note is and is not. It is not a grievance. Nobody in this directorate acted in bad faith, and I am not asking anyone to explain themselves. What I am recording is that the concern was unspoken, that the summary we all read glossed over it in half a sentence, and that we let it slide for eleven weeks because no meeting owned it.

Two changes from October. First, reserving becomes a standing item on the monthly call, with a named owner in Brazil and one in Milan. Second, anyone who has a misgiving about a number brings it to that call, unfinished. I would rather absorb the friction of a difficult ten minutes every month than course-correct twice a year in front of the board. I wish this had been the arrangement in June. It is the arrangement now.
reading.source: Quarterly retrospective -- circulated to regional leadership

gist.prompt: What is this retrospective mainly recording?
choices: The reasons the quarter closed four points below plan
Why a problem that was visible in June was never said out loud, and what changes because of it
A complaint about the colleagues who saw the reserving gap and stayed quiet

items: The reserving gap was hidden from the leadership.

From October, reserving will be discussed at every monthly call.
